directions.title: Pay for reach on what already works
directions.plain: Put ad money behind your best existing posts, aimed at women 25-34 in the US. You keep posting 3 to 5 times a week. Fast, but it moves with ad prices.
directions.why_for_you: On-hand shots are your best post type, and your ad weeks have landed inside the engine's range, while October's creator posts did not arrive.
directions.you_would_do: Pick your 2 best on-hand posts, set a daily cap between $120 and $260 for the month, keep the posting rhythm.

directions.title: Send pieces to small creators
directions.plain: Ship 4 to 8 pieces to small creators your customer already follows. They shoot the wearing shots you cannot. Slow to start, and some will not post.
directions.why_for_you: October is the evidence here: only 1 of 4 creators posted, so the engine now trusts this direction less until the post rate improves.
directions.you_would_do: Send 6 to 8 DMs in week 1, ship by week 2, repost what comes back.
directions.caution: October post rate was 1 of 4. The engine now assumes 49% and attacks this direction with no-shows first.

directions.title: Just post, steadily
directions.plain: No spend. Post 4 to 5 times a week, mostly on-hand and close-up shots. Keeps the account warm and saves the budget.
directions.why_for_you: On-hand is your best post type, so steady posting never wastes money, but it is slow.
directions.you_would_do: Make 16 to 20 posts this month. That is all.
directions.caution: On your numbers this does not reach the order goal alone.

directions.title: Run a one-week sale
directions.plain: A discount week pulls orders forward. It works once in a while; done often it trains people to wait.
directions.why_for_you: Nothing in your history shows a sale working yet, so this is the least proven choice for you.
directions.you_would_do: Pick one week, announce it, discount 10 to 20 percent, and ship the spike.
directions.caution: Your history has only two sale weeks, and the engine's sale-week estimate is its weakest.
